newsitem.title: UK: ICCO accord sees cocoa cut of 15,000 tonnes 96/97.
newsitem.headline: ICCO accord sees cocoa cut of 15,000 tonnes 96/97.

text.p: An International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) accord on Thursday to set a target cocoa stock-to-grind ratio at 34 percent is likely to mean an agreed goal of a cut of just 15,000 tonnes in projected 1996/97 output. A committee of the ICCO at London talks on Thursday agreed to set a target of 34 percent for the world stock/grind ratio as of the end of the 1998/99 crop year, delegates said.

This must be endorsed on Friday by an ICCO council session which will then set goals for curbing output for the next three years according to secretariat scenarios based on the accepted stock/grind ratio.

The scenario based on a 34 percent ratio is for a cut of 90,000 tonnes over three years. The ICCO would aim to reduce by 15,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 October-December crop year, by 30,000 the next year and by 45,000 in the third.

This formula, which delegates said was likely to be agreed, would be the smallest cut in any secretariat scenario. For instance, at a target ratio of 28 percent, cuts would be 70,000 then 140,000 and finally 210,000 tonnes.
"We feel that the (agreed) ratio is least destructive to the market," said a spokesman for consumers who had prevailed over producer calls for a different ratio.
